note: The paper behind the main attention-free alternative, worth knowing when a client stack is not transformer based.
title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

reading.body:
Mamba is a credible non-attention alternative to the Transformer, with 9,139 citations and reported inference five times faster than Transformers.

The pattern is a sequence model whose cost grows with sequence length rather than exploding with it. That makes long inputs practical, and the paper reports gains on data up to million-length sequences across language, audio, and genomics. A 3 billion parameter Mamba beats Transformers of equal size and matches Transformers with double the parameters.

For AI specifically, this matters because attention is the part of the stack that makes long context expensive to serve. If a model can decide what to keep and discard as it reads, the compute needed per token of context falls, and the same building and power budget serves more work. The note attached to this paper frames it as the thing to know when a client stack is not transformer based.

What the data does not cover is adoption. Citation count measures attention from researchers, not deployment in production systems. The performance claims are the paper's own, and the entry carries no independent benchmark, no cost measurement on real hardware, and no comparison against newer architectures. It is a 2023 preprint, and the field has moved since.

explain_beginner: Most AI systems for language and other sequences use a design called the Transformer. The paper presents Mamba, a design that avoids attention. Mamba can decide what to keep or forget as it reads each item in a sequence, which helps with language and discrete data. It runs faster than Transformers, five times more work per second, and its cost grows steadily as inputs get longer, so long inputs become practical. It performs well on language, audio, and genomics. A 3 billion parameter Mamba does better than Transformers of equal size and equals Transformers with double the parameters. This matters because teams may not need attention models for every task.
explain_business: For executives, Mamba is an alternative to systems built on Transformers, especially when long inputs or inference cost matter. The paper reports faster inference, five times more work per second than Transformers, and cost that rises with sequence length, so longer documents or signals do not become expensive. It works across language, audio, and genomics. In language, a 3 billion parameter Mamba beats Transformers of equal size and matches Transformers with double the parameters. The decision this informs is to evaluate Mamba for workloads where context length, latency, or throughput are constraints, rather than assuming every AI stack must use attention. It may reduce serving costs and expand use cases.
explain_practitioner: This work addresses a weakness in subquadratic sequence models: they cannot reason from content. They make model parameters depend on the input, so the model can decide what information to carry forward and what to discard across the sequence. They design a hardware aware parallel method in recurrent form. These selective models form Mamba, a network design without attention or MLP blocks. Mamba gives inference five times faster than Transformers, cost that rises with sequence length, and gains on data up to million length sequences. It works across language, audio, and genomics. A 3 billion parameter Mamba beats Transformers of equal size and matches Transformers with double the parameters.
